title: Grammar and Sentence Structure
summary: Clauses and sentence types, concord, tenses, active and passive voice, direct and reported speech, punctuation for meaning, and common errors tested in Paper 1 Section C.

rows: Two main clauses joined by a coordinating conjunction
The committee met, but no decision was taken.
Although the committee met, no decision was taken.
Two or more main clauses + at least one subordinate clause
When the results arrived, the learners cheered and the teachers smiled.

items: **Adjectival (relative) clause**: describes a noun: *The book **that I borrowed** is overdue.*
**Adverbial clause**: tells when, why, how, under what condition: *We left **because it was raining**.*
**Noun clause**: acts as subject or object: ***What she said** surprised everyone.*
*Neither the principal nor the teachers **were** present.* (verb agrees with the nearer subject)
*Each of the candidates **has** a number.* (each is singular)
*The number of complaints **has** risen.* / *A number of learners **have** complained.*

rows: The minister has announced new measures.
New measures have been announced by the minister.
The road was being blocked by protesters.

notes.title: Reported speech
notes.problem: 'We will publish the results tomorrow,' the official said.
steps: we → they; will → would; tomorrow → the next day.
notes.answer: The official said that they would publish the results the next day.

rows: Me and him went to the match.
He and I went to the match.
Being a rainy day, the match was cancelled. (dangling modifier)
Because it was a rainy day, the match was cancelled.

notes.label: Exam tip
notes.text: Paper 1 Section C often asks you to correct an error, change voice or speech, combine sentences, or identify parts of speech in an advert or cartoon. Rewrite the whole sentence correctly; do not only fix one word unless asked.

options: The bus was late, so we walked.
Because the bus was late, we walked.

questions.prompt: Identify the type of clause in bold: 'The learner **who won the prize** is my cousin.'
Choose the correct verb: 'Neither the players nor the coach ___ happy with the result.'
Choose the correct verb: 'The number of applicants ___ increased.'
'Between you and I' is grammatically correct.
Rewrite in the passive voice: 'The municipality will repair the potholes next week.'
questions.memo:
✓ The potholes will be repaired (1)
✓ by the municipality next week. (1)

questions.prompt: Rewrite in reported speech: 'I am preparing my speech now,' said Thandi.
questions.memo:
✓ Thandi said that she (1)
✓ was preparing her speech (1)
✓ then. (1)

questions.prompt: Correct the dangling modifier: 'Walking into the hall, the noise was deafening.'
questions.memo: ✓✓ e.g. 'As I walked into the hall, I found the noise deafening.' / 'Walking into the hall, we heard a deafening noise.' (2)

questions.prompt: Combine into one complex sentence using a relative pronoun: 'The novel won an award. It was written by a South African author.'
questions.memo: ✓✓ 'The novel, which was written by a South African author, won an award.' (2)

questions.prompt: Correct the THREE errors: 'Less learners attended the meeting, and the reason is because it's time was changed.'
questions.memo:
✓ Fewer learners (1)
✓ the reason is that (1)
✓ its time (1)
